correctness.rationale: Uniform marks thin the clocks into two exclusive rates lambda-c and one common rate c=lambda(m-1)/(N-1); joint no-reset intervals yield exp[-lambda(u+v)+c min(u,v)] below the horizon. Capping each backward time at t gives precisely the initial zero start and includes the atom at t. Conditional on ages the Brownian squared radii are independent 2DA_i times chi-square_d, giving strictly positive tail derivatives for positive arguments and thresholds. Layer cake yields the displayed strictly positive comparison on a rectangle of positive area for every t>0; fixed marginals and bivariate upper-orthant order give concordance/supermodular order, also after independent increasing scale mixtures. For the conditional result, below the observed age b<a the second age can be cut off only by its exclusive clock; for b>a an exclusive mark at a is required for label 1 and the second clock then has total rate lambda before a. At the horizon atom and complete synchrony these formulas have the asserted limiting meaning. The increase of the conditional age kernel on b between distinct observed ages implies strict increase for g_y(a). The posterior likelihood ratio for z2>z1 is strictly increasing in a on a nondegenerate age support; positive covariance of this ratio with g_y gives strict regression for the density-defined version on z>0. Independent signs give opposite signed-quadrant comparisons in one dimension and likewise for any scalar coordinate in higher dimensions. Integrating age survival and the first two chi-square moments gives the frozen covariances, including c=0 and c=lambda. My bounded reproduction, python /workspace/branches/replay_frozen.py 1, used conditioning on the exclusive/common mark at a rather than double age-survival integration; the six anchor tails agree within 1.4e-9, and it checks a nontrivial posterior grid and independent endpoints. The simulation and quadrature in the source are recorded evidence, not proofs or runs performed here.
